title: Infosys Q1 Profit Jumps 12% but Trimmed Growth Outlook Signals Caution
excerpt: India's second-largest IT firm posted strong earnings and surging AI revenue, but narrowed its FY27 guidance amid an uneven macro environment and named a new CEO to steer the company through an industry-wide AI transition.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Infosys Q1 FY27 net profit rose 12.2% to ₹7,769 crore ($820 million).
  • FY27 revenue growth guidance narrowed to 1.5%–3.0%, below analyst expectations.
  • AI services now contribute 8.2% of revenue, up from 5.5% in December.
  • Ashiss Kumar Dash named new CEO, effective April 2027, succeeding Salil Parekh.

Earnings Beat on Profit, Miss on Revenue

Infosys (NSE: INFY) on July 23 reported a 12.2% jump in consolidated net profit to ₹7,769 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up from ₹6,921 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 14% to ₹48,211 crore ($5.08 billion), though both figures came in slightly below analyst expectations of ₹7,832 crore and ₹4,836.7 crore respectively, according to data compiled by LSEG.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=2S6tbyRxQPM

In constant-currency terms, revenue grew 2.4% year-on-year and 1.0% sequentially. Operating margin improved to 21.1%, up 30 basis points from a year ago. Earnings per share grew 14.9% year-on-year in rupee terms, while free cash flow came in at $955 million — a conversion rate of 116.5% of net profit.

On a sequential basis, however, net profit declined 8.6% from ₹8,501 crore in the previous quarter, reflecting what CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka described as a one-time revenue impact from a client decision and softer-than-expected volume.

Guidance Trimmed as Macro Remains Uneven

The headline change was the narrowing of Infosys's FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to a range of 1.5%–3.0%, down from the earlier 1.5%–3.5%. The 50-basis-point trim to the upper end may seem modest, but it undershot analyst expectations of 2.5%–4.5% growth for the full year.

"The upper end of the guidance had previously assumed an improving macro environment in the second half, but conditions now appear a little bit more uneven."

— Salil Parekh, CEO & Managing Director, Infosys

Sanghrajka added that the cascading effect of the Q1 one-off, combined with the expected Q4 impact from a European manufacturing client deal that Infosys chose not to pursue, would weigh on the full-year outlook. Operating margin guidance was retained at 20%–22%.

The cautious stance contrasts with rivals Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech, which both beat quarterly estimates earlier this month, aided by strong financial services demand and a weaker rupee.

AI Revenue Surges Past 8%

A bright spot was the acceleration in AI-linked revenue. AI services accounted for 8.2% of Infosys's total revenue in Q1, up sharply from 5.5% in the December quarter — a figure Sanghrajka called "already significant" and clarified was not due to reclassification.

CEO Parekh said AI momentum is "rapidly converting into revenue" through six growth areas, including agentic process automation, data modernization, and coding tools. More than 80,000 employees now use coding tools for client and internal work, and the company plans to build a team of 6,000 "frontier engineers" over the coming years.

Large deal total contract value stood at $3.6 billion for the quarter, with 61% classified as net new business, up from $3.2 billion in Q4 but below the $3.8 billion booked in the year-ago period. Six of the large deals were consolidation wins worth $700 million in net new business.

New CEO for an AI-Driven Era

Alongside the results, Infosys announced that company veteran Ashiss Kumar Dash will succeed Parekh as CEO and Managing Director, effective April 1, 2027, for a five-year term. Parekh, who has led Infosys since 2018 and doubled its revenue from $10 billion to over $20 billion, will step down on March 31, 2027. A formal mentoring period begins October 1.

Dash, a 31-year Infosys veteran who currently heads the energy vertical and is based in Los Angeles, was described by co-founder and Chairman Nandan Nilekani as a "true blue Infoscion."

"Ashiss Kumar Dash is a safe, execution-focused appointment at a time when Infosys needs stability as much as transformation."

— Phil Fersht, CEO, HFS Research

What It Means for the Indian IT Workforce

For the global Indian diaspora, the results carry direct implications. Infosys employs over 300,000 people worldwide and is among the largest sponsors of H-1B visas in the United States. Its guidance on hiring — 20,000 college graduates planned for this fiscal year, with over 4,000 already recruited in Q1 — offers a concrete signal on the health of Indian IT employment pipelines.

The company's pivot toward AI, including its 6,000-strong frontier engineer initiative, also signals a shift in the skill sets that will drive future hiring. Parekh noted that AI and productivity improvements have boosted revenue productivity, though pricing compression in parts of the portfolio remains a headwind.

From a sector standpoint, Infosys's cautious guidance — even as AI revenue surges — reflects a broader reality for Indian IT: the AI transition is generating new revenue streams but has yet to fully offset macro-driven softness in traditional services. Financial services and energy remain bright spots, while retail and communications continue to face pressure.

What's Next

Infosys shares fell about 3% in early U.S. trading following the results. Investors will watch whether the AI revenue trajectory sustains its double-digit sequential growth and how the CEO transition unfolds in the coming quarters. The company's next earnings are expected in October 2026.
